name: browserwright-remote
label: browserwright (remote CloakBrowser)
_note: Same one-shot `browserwright markdown` as the `browserwright` rung, but the
throwaway session ATTACHES to a remote CDP endpoint instead of using your
Chrome: BW_REMOTE_CDP is a ws(s):// or http(s):// URL (an http(s) one is
resolved through its /json/version). The executor stays local; only the
browser is remote. The browser is borrowed, so it is left running on end.
Inert until BW_REMOTE_CDP is set: an unset variable reports `missing env
BW_REMOTE_CDP` and the chain moves on without spawning anything.
Ordered after the local rung and before `raw`: it is the fallback for when
your Chrome is unavailable, and it must precede `raw` because raw accepts
text/html verbatim and would otherwise always win. To make it primary, move
No login state: it is someone else's (anti-detect) browser profile, so pages
behind your logins come back as their logged-out versions.
timeoutMs is 240s because the endpoint may QUEUE the connection (hold the ws
handshake) for a couple of minutes when its concurrency limit is reached,
and starts the browser lazily on first connect.
